raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Part of #63818 (RFC: pluggable PP transport), the "re-prefill" hook. Adds `KVConnectorOutput.lost_kv_req_ids` and `lost_all_kv`, so a worker, connector or executor can report KV that was computed and then lost on some worker (for example a pipeline stage replaced by a replica that does not hold it); the scheduler then recomputes the affected running requests. Independent of the other #63818 PRs (based on main).

## Claims

- With `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute` (and without a KV transfer config) the scheduler preempts the reported running requests with `drop_stale_output=True` (the path `reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)` already uses): their in-flight outputs are dropped and they resume with a prefill of all their tokens (with MRV2, as `NewRequestData` carrying all token ids).
- Their blocks (with `lost_all_kv`: all blocks) are evicted from the prefix cache first. Without this the resumed request, or a new request with the same prefix, hits blocks whose KV is missing on that worker, and decodes on a partial context.
- With `kv_load_failure_policy=fail` the requests finish with an error. `KVOutputAggregator` merges both fields across workers.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -v     # 25 passed (6 new)
pre-commit run --files <changed files>               # pass
```

- `test_lost_kv_recomputes_with_inflight_output[pp_size=1,3][lost_all]`: drives a real `AsyncScheduler` with the existing `PipelinedEngine` harness (up to `pp_size` steps in flight) and reports lost KV at two steps; every request finishes with exactly `max_tokens` tokens, delivered tokens are an ordered subset of what the runner sampled, each token sits at the sequence position it was sampled for, every lost request is resumed with all its tokens, and no stale share is left.
- `test_lost_kv_evicts_prefix_cache`: with prefix caching on, a lost request resumes with `num_computed_tokens == 0` (it fails without the eviction).
- `test_lost_kv_fails_requests_under_fail_policy`.

End to end (with the out-of-process stage PRs of #63818 and the Connex plugin, Llama-3-8B, PP=2 and PP=3, A40, SIGKILL of the active downstream replica under load): 28 kills in total. Under load (14 kills: PP=2 on one host x10, last stage of PP=3 x2, PP=2 with the stages on two hosts x2): 4,448 of 4,448 requests completed, 0 errors, all 32 requests in flight at each kill resumed; the largest gap between two tokens of a request was 0.39-0.71 s per run. During 16-request greedy runs (14 kills): 13 runs completed with 0 tokens off the argmax; in one run (PP=2, one host, 4th kill of a series) all 16 requests hung until the client timeout. It did not reproduce in 15 later kills and its logs were overwritten, so the cause is unknown; it is in the plugin's failover path or in this change, not yet determined. Before the prefix-cache eviction was added, the same kill left 59 tokens off the argmax in 14 of 16 requests, all after the failover point (tokens 82-91), which is how the eviction requirement was found.

## Details

- Why not `invalid_block_ids`: it rewinds a request only to its first invalid block among tokens computed before the current step, keeps the outputs of the current and in-flight steps (with async scheduling / PP several steps are in flight), and under the recompute policy leaves the invalid blocks in the prefix cache. Lost KV needs all three handled.
- Why preemption: it already handles in-flight outputs (stale shares) for async scheduling and PP, and MRV2 resumes preempted requests as new requests with all their tokens, so a worker that never saw the request gets its full context.
- Cost: nothing unless a field is set. On a report, O(running requests) plus an eviction pass over the reported blocks (all blocks for `lost_all_kv`).
- Who sets it: today an executor (the Connex PP executor sets `lost_all_kv` on the first output after it replaced a downstream stage replica). A worker-side connector method can follow if connectors need it; the aggregator already merges the fields.
- Not a duplicate: open PRs on KV load failures (#61769, #53298, #42461) change `invalid_block_ids` handling for connectors; none covers KV lost after it was computed.

Developed with AI coding assistance; all changes were reviewed and tested by the author.

🚀

More end-to-end runs with this change (no code change in this PR).

With the out-of-process stages of #63898 and the Connex plugin (same-host hops now over CUDA IPC), killing a downstream stage replica under 32 streaming clients: PP=2, 5 kills, 3,968 of 3,968 requests completed, 0 errors, all 32 in-flight requests resumed each time, largest token gap 0.34-0.60 s per run; PP=3 with the **middle** stage killed, 2 kills, 576/576, gaps 0.69 and 2.61 s. Greedy correctness runs with a kill: 0 tokens off the argmax in all completed runs (teacher-forced on a non-PP instance). For comparison, stock vLLM with NCCL PP=2 and a supervisor that restarts it loses all 32 in-flight requests and is down 57-63 s per kill (3 kills).

Single host, few repetitions (2-5 kills per configuration); the comparison is about behaviour (requests survive vs fail), not a tuned latency number.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

### 🟡 Changes recommended Recovery leaves gaps for waiting requests and departed owners, and eviction incorrectly mixes block IDs from independent cache pools.
3 open issues - [Recover waiting requests after complete KV cache loss](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63899#discussion_r4384313354) · New - [Invalidate cache when KV loss reports outlive request state](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63899#discussion_r4384313399) · New - [Evict HiSparse blocks through their owning cache pools](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63899#discussion_r4384313418) · New
What changed in this PR Adds a worker-reported KV-cache loss signal to support request recovery after pipeline-stage replacement, providing the re-prefill hook proposed in #63818. **Changes:** - Adds per-request and whole-cache loss fields and merges reports across workers. - Handles reported loss through cache eviction and request recomputation or failure. - Adds recovery tests and clarifies the failure-policy docstring. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `vllm/​v1/​outputs.py` | Defines loss-report fields and updates empty-output detection. | | `vllm/​v1/​core/​sched/​scheduler.py` | Handles loss reports, eviction, and request recovery. | | `vllm/​distributed/​kv_transfer/​kv_connector/​utils.py` | Aggregates loss reports across workers. | | `vllm/​config/​kv_transfer.py` | Documents how the existing failure policy applies to lost KV. | | `tests/​v1/​core/​test_async_scheduler.py` | Tests in-flight recovery, failure handling, and prefix-cache eviction. |
Review effort: Balanced

With `lost_all_kv=True`, KV-holding waiting requests such as paused streaming sessions retain their block tables and nonzero `num_computed_tokens`. Evicting their prefix-cache hashes does not reset those references, so the next input resumes against KV the replacement worker no longer holds. Recover these requests while preserving their blocked/session state, or finish them with an error under the fail policy.

All three are fixed in 1852248f (on top of the PR commit rebased onto current main, 563bf82b).

Confirmed and fixed. `_handle_lost_kv` now also covers requests in `kv_holding_waiting` (when reported by ID, or all of them with `lost_all_kv`). A waiting request that holds computed KV, such as a paused streaming session, has its blocks freed and evicted and `num_computed_tokens` reset to 0, and it moves to the waiting queue in order. Its status is kept, so a paused session stays in `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` and its next input runs a prefill of all its tokens. @@ -811,3 +811,267 @@ def test_resumable_request_handoff():
 
     engine._process_oldest_step()
     assert len(request.output_token_ids) == 1
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("lost_all", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("pp_size", [1, 3])
+def test_lost_kv_recomputes_with_inflight_output(pp_size: int, lost_all: bool):
+    """KVConnectorOutput.lost_kv_req_ids preempts the requests (their KV is
+    gone on some worker): in-flight output is dropped, they resume with a
+    prefill of all their tokens, and the delivered tokens stay consistent."""
+    from vllm.v1.outputs import KVConnectorOutput
+
+    max_tokens = 24
+    scheduler = _create_async_pp_scheduler(num_spec=0, pp_size=pp_size, num_blocks=64)
+    requests = create_requests(
+        num_requests=6, num_tokens=8, max_tokens=max_tokens, ignore_eos=True
+    )
+    for req in requests:
+        scheduler.add_request(req)
+
+    lost_steps = {5, 12}
+    lost: set[str] = set()
+    processed = 0
+    orig_update = scheduler.update_from_output
+
+    def update_from_output(scheduler_output, model_runner_output):
+        nonlocal processed
+        processed += 1
+        if processed in lost_steps:
+            # E.g. a downstream pipeline stage was replaced: every running
+            # request lost its KV there.
+            ids = {req.request_id for req in scheduler.running}
+            lost.update(ids)
+            model_runner_output.kv_connector_output = (
+                KVConnectorOutput(lost_all_kv=True)
+                if lost_all
+                else KVConnectorOutput(lost_kv_req_ids=ids)
+            )
+        return orig_update(scheduler_output, model_runner_output)
+
+    scheduler.update_from_output = update_from_output
+    resumed_with_all_tokens = []
+    orig_schedule = scheduler.schedule
+
+    def schedule():
+        output = orig_schedule()
+        for new_req in output.scheduled_new_reqs:
+            if new_req.num_computed_tokens == 0 and len(new_req.prefill_token_ids) > 8:
+                resumed_with_all_tokens.append(new_req.req_id)
+        return output
+
+    scheduler.schedule = schedule
+    engine = PipelinedEngine(scheduler, queue_size=pp_size + 1)
+    engine.run()

+    def _handle_lost_kv(self, lost_req_ids: set[str], lost_all: bool) -> set[str]:
+        """Handle running requests whose KV cache was lost on some worker.
+
+        Their blocks (with lost_all: all blocks) are evicted from the prefix
+        cache, since what they hold is no longer valid everywhere. With the
+        recompute policy the requests are preempted, so they resume with a
+        prefill of all their tokens and their in-flight outputs are dropped.
+        Returns the IDs of the requests to fail (fail policy).
+        """
+        lost_reqs = [
+            req for req in self.running if lost_all or req.request_id in lost_req_ids
+        ]
+        if lost_all:
+            blocks_to_evict = set(
+                range(self.kv_cache_manager.block_pool.num_gpu_blocks)
+            )
+        else:
+            blocks_to_evict = {
+                block_id
+                for req in lost_reqs
+                for group in self.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(req.request_id)
+                for block_id in group
+            }
+        self.kv_cache_manager.evict_blocks(blocks_to_evict)

All three are fixed in 1852248f (on top of the PR commit rebased onto current main, 563bf82b).

Confirmed and fixed. `_handle_lost_kv` now also covers requests in `kv_holding_waiting` (when reported by ID, or all of them with `lost_all_kv`). A waiting request that holds computed KV, such as a paused streaming session, has its blocks freed and evicted and `num_computed_tokens` reset to 0, and it moves to the waiting queue in order. Its status is kept, so a paused session stays in `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` and its next input runs a prefill of all its tokens. An async load that is still in flight (`WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`) is marked as a failed receive, so it is recomputed once it reports completion. Under `kv_load_failure_policy=fail` these requests finish with an error, and `num_waiting_for_streaming_input` is kept consistent. Tests: `test_lost_kv_resets_paused_streaming_session[lost_all=False/True]`, `test_lost_kv_fails_paused_streaming_session_under_fail_policy`, `test_lost_all_kv_retries_inflight_async_load`.

Confirmed and fixed. The scheduler no longer passes `get_block_ids()` to `evict_blocks()`. The new `KVCacheManager.evict_request_blocks(request_id)` evicts each KV cache group's blocks through that group's own `block_pool` (HiSparse's host group has its own pool), and `evict_all_cached_blocks()` evicts every distinct pool once, which replaces the earlier `range(num_gpu_blocks)` that only covered the GPU pool. Test: `test_lost_kv_evicts_blocks_through_their_owning_pool`.

Without the fix, the five new tests in `test_async_scheduler.py` and the new test in `test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py` fail. With it, `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`, `test_scheduler.py`, `test_prefix_caching.py` and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py` plus `test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py` pass (551 tests).

More end-to-end runs with this change (no code change in this PR).

With the out-of-process stages of #63898 and the Connex plugin (same-host hops now over CUDA IPC), killing a downstream stage replica under 32 streaming clients: PP=2, 5 kills, 3,968 of 3,968 requests completed, 0 errors, all 32 in-flight requests resumed each time, largest token gap 0.34-0.60 s per run; PP=3 with the **middle** stage killed, 2 kills, 576/576, gaps 0.69 and 2.61 s. Greedy correctness runs with a kill: 0 tokens off the argmax in all completed runs (teacher-forced on a non-PP instance). For comparison, stock vLLM with NCCL PP=2 and a supervisor that restarts it loses all 32 in-flight requests and is down 57-63 s per kill (3 kills).

Single host, few repetitions (2-5 kills per configuration); the comparison is about behaviour (requests survive vs fail), not a tuned latency number.
